griefer transfers 1 ether USDT directly to uniswapV2Pair (USDT.transfer(pair, 1e18)) -- NO mint, just a donation
Now USDT.balanceOf(pair) >= r0_USDT + 1 ether ==> _isAddLiquidity() returns true
victim seller calls router.swapExactTokensForTokens(...path=[LAXO,USDT]...)
Inside LAXOToken._transfer the recipient==uniswapV2Pair branch hits `if (_isAddLiquidity()) revert('add liquidity not allowed');`

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: // PancakeRouter._swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens reads reserveThis = X via getReserves() BEFORE invoking ESTToken._transfer(attacker, pair, amount). During _transfer with from = attacker (not in ammPairs), the contract calls autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens() at L446 which executes _tOwned[uniswapV2Pair] = _tOwned[uniswapV2Pair].sub(amountToBurn) and IUniswapV2Pair(uniswapV2Pair).sync() at L555 — driving the pair's recorded reserveThis from X down to X - amountToBurn (reserveOther unchanged). Router then re-reads pair.balanceOf(EST) - reserveThis_post_sync = transferAmount and calls getAmountOut(transferAmount, reserveThis_post_sync, reserveOther) = getAmountOut(transferAmount, X - amountToBurn, reserveOther). Since AMM output is strictly monotonically decreasing in reserveIn, the attacker's awardToken receipt strictly exceeds the fair-swap output getAmountOut(transferAmount, X, reserveOther). Wei delta scales with amountToBurn = (pairBalance * percentForLPBurn / 10000), i.e. ≈0.08% of pair's EST balance per cycle — small per-tx but free-running and chainable across lpBurnFrequency windows. ALSO: the _pendingSellBurn path (L419-437) provides a SECOND sync: after the sell, attacker triggers any non-buy transfer, draining up to pairBalance/10 EST from the pair AND calling sync, set up for a follow-up profitable buy/sell cycle. attack_steps: Wait until block.timestamp >= lastLpBurnTime + lpBurnFrequency (default 3600s) so autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens will execute its burn branch.

Attacker calls router.swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens with path [EST, awardToken]. Router transferFrom's EST from attacker to pair, which invokes ESTToken._transfer(attacker, pair, amount).

Inside _transfer: !ammPairs[attacker] is true, so autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens() runs at L446 — computes amountToBurn = pair_EST_balance * 8 / 10000, halves it, debits _tOwned[pair] by amountToBurn, debits _tTotal by halfBurn, credits halfToWallet to burnReceiver, and calls IUniswapV2Pair(pair).sync(). reserveThis is now X - amountToBurn while reserveOther is unchanged.
Sell branch then executes (takeFee = true since attacker not excluded): _tOwned[attacker].sub(amount); _tOwned[pair].add(transferAmount = 0.95*amount); _pendingSellBurn += transferAmount.

Control returns to PancakeRouter, which computes amountInput = pair.balanceOf(EST) - reserveThis_post_sync = transferAmount, then amountOutput = getAmountOut(transferAmount, X - amountToBurn, reserveOther). Calls pair.swap(...) sending awardToken to attacker.

Attacker awardToken received strictly > fair-swap output getAmountOut(transferAmount, X, reserveOther) by Δ ≈ transferAmount * 997 * amountToBurn * reserveOther / [(1000*X + 997*transferAmount)(1000*(X - amountToBurn) + 997*transferAmount)] (positive).

Optionally: in a follow-up tx attacker triggers the _pendingSellBurn branch (any non-buy transfer of EST) which burns up to pairBalance/10 EST + sync(), inflating EST price further; then attacker buys cheaply or sells additional inventory at the inflated rate. Free-running attack — repeat across lpBurnFrequency windows until _tTotal hits minSupply (= 130k EST).

setup_calls: STEP A — seed _pendingSellBurn: attacker sells `sellAmount` EST via router. Inside _transfer with takeFee=true and isSell=true (ammPairs[to] && !isAddLdx), the contract does _pendingSellBurn += transferAmount (= 0.95 * sellAmount, L510). Note: the autoBurnLiquidityPairTokens path also fires if frequency elapsed, but is independent.

STEP B — trigger drain: in the SAME or NEXT block attacker initiates ANY non-buy transfer of EST (e.g. attacker.transfer(self, 1) or attacker → some EOA). _transfer's L419 branch runs because _pendingSellBurn > 0 and !ammPairs[from]. burnAmount = _pendingSellBurn, capped at pairBalance/10 (L423). _tOwned[uniswapV2Pair] -= burnAmount, _tTotal -= burnAmount, IUniswapV2Pair(pair).sync().

post_vuln_state.custom_assertion: // After STEP B, the pair's reserveThis has been deflated by burnAmount (up to 10% of pre-burn pair EST) and sync() locked it in. Attacker now executes STEP C: a buy of awardToken → EST through the router (or, equivalently, a flash-loaned awardToken sell into EST then immediate sell back). Because reserveThis dropped while reserveOther stayed flat, the EST/awardToken price quoted by the AMM is now skewed: the pair's k-product is X*reserveOther → (X - burnAmount)*reserveOther. Subsequent swaps see a more advantageous quote depending on direction. The cleanest profit chain (when attacker holds idle EST off-pair): STEP C = sell more EST at the now-deflated reserveThis — getAmountOut(amountIn, X - burnAmount, reserveOther) > getAmountOut(amountIn, X, reserveOther). Wei delta dominated by burnAmount/X ratio; with the 10% cap on a fresh pair this is ≈11% reserve deflation per single trigger, vastly larger than the autoBurn 0.08%/cycle of holdout_est_baseline-1. Profit oracle: attacker awardToken receipt across STEP A+STEP C combined exceeds the counterfactual two-sells-on-same-initial-reserves yield. min_profit_wei conservatively 1e16 awardToken-wei. Critically, the burn-and-sync runs WITHOUT the router being aware (this is between two router invocations), so no balance-vs-reserve delta is reconciled — the price manipulation is durable across the attacker's next swap.

attack_steps: STEP A: attacker sells sellAmount EST via PancakeRouter swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens. ESTToken._transfer(attacker, pair, sellAmount): takeFee branch runs, transferAmount = 0.95*sellAmount lands at pair, _pendingSellBurn = transferAmount (L510). Router collects fair awardToken output for this sell.

STEP B (the bug-trigger): in a follow-up tx (or even the same block via a multicall contract) attacker calls EST.transfer(<any non-pair EOA>, 1 wei). _transfer enters with from = attacker (not in ammPairs) and _pendingSellBurn > 0 → L419 branch executes. burnAmount = min(_pendingSellBurn, _tOwned[pair]/10). _tOwned[pair] -= burnAmount, _tTotal -= burnAmount, pair.sync(). reserveThis is now (X + transferAmount_from_step_A) - burnAmount, but since burnAmount can equal up to ~95% of the just-deposited transferAmount (capped by 10% of post-A pair balance), reserveThis is meaningfully below STEP-A's post-trade level — i.e. the pair has been silently drained.

STEP C: attacker (or accomplice) executes a second sell (or a buy followed by sell within the same block) using the artificially-low reserveThis. getAmountOut(secondAmountIn, reserveThis_post_drain, reserveOther) returns more awardToken than fair. ALSO: each STEP-C sell re-seeds _pendingSellBurn, allowing the cycle to repeat until _tTotal converges to minSupply (130k EST).

Optionally chain: the attack also composes with a flash loan of awardToken — buy EST in step A's wake (consuming the deflation), force burn-and-sync via STEP B, dump on the depressed reserveThis. Net awardToken delta strictly positive when 0.05% router fee and 5% transfer fee combined are smaller than the swap-quote uplift, which holds for burnAmount/X above ~6% (easily achieved at the 10% cap).
preconditions: Attacker can issue two transfers: one router sell (STEP A) and one direct EST.transfer (STEP B) — both available to any EOA
Attacker is not in _isExcludedFromFee[] (i.e. ANY adversary EOA satisfies this; only the deployer / contract / DEAD / burnReceiver are excluded by default)
_tTotal > minSupply (130k ether) — bug self-disables when total burns down to floor, but the floor is 0.01% of initial supply, so attack window is enormous
Standard PancakeSwap V2 router on BSC mainnet (0x10ED43...024E) — pair created via factory in constructor
